contexts.text: A robber who preferred to stay in urinous tuns. SE 1160.
The deceitful... seem to dwell in a tun... called the infernal tun. Described. SE 285. (They remain in it for ages. SE 286.)
There is another tun, also at the left, in which are some who had supposed that when they did evil they did good, and the converse. They remain there for a while.
The worst of the Spirits of Jupiter are kept as it were in a tun. Described.
There was then represented to me a certain tun, almost like the infernal tun. Explained.
When (these tenaciously revengeful Spirits) come into view, there appears a large and wide tun of a brown colour, in which they are kept... for they suppose that they rule the universe from it.
Thus the province of the colon extends to Hell, or the infernal tun, as the colon does to the rectum, which is the infernal tun.

The hypocritical Spirit is then inverted with his head in a tun; but is raised up again with the tun upon his head, which he labours to remove from himself, but in vain; and when he is liberated, he is again involved in the tun...
Those who had wanted to be first in everything... are in an infernal tun; but still these are not evil...
I saw three or four trees planted in a kind of tun. (This tun is called in the parallel passage, AC 5051, a wooden receptacle.)
I saw a kind of tun, or mortar... and a man pitched human flesh (and thus men) into that tun... SE 3658. SE 3659.
Lejel was sent into a chamber-pot or tun of urine, which he did not fear.
He was again sent into the urinary tun, and there seemed as if he had come into his Heaven.
